text:
sara: Ran an end-to-end nsys capture on a 16-GPU run to investigate tail latency. Seeing repeated hostspin / CPU-sched gaps that serialize H2D memcpys and break overlap with kernels. trace: https://s3.redwood/traces/1798765432/nsys/index.html

devon: can you paste the waterfall snippet or a short timeline gif? which thread is doing the prefetch?

sara: pasted a 2s waterfall clip into the trace link above. pattern is: prefetch thread issues async H2D on stream 4, kernel launches on stream 0, but CPU shows a 0.8-1.5ms wakeup gap between them, causing memcpy backlog. sample lines:```
[stream=4] cudaMemcpyAsync H2D 18us
CPU sched gap 1.2ms (hostspin sleeping)
[stream=0] kernel conv_fwd 720us (stalled start)
```

nate: that sounds like the KV-cache prefetch thread (it does pinned allocs + cudaMemcpyAsync). are we sure copy engine vs compute stream mapping isn't colliding?

sara: yep it's the kv-prefetch worker. interestingly on a few traces I saw memcpy actually overlap kernels when the kernel was on stream 1 and the copy on stream 3, so stream assignment matters.

eva: two hypotheses: 1) OS CPU preemption of the prefetch thread -> delayed cudaMemcpyAsync submission, 2) our batcher is producing many small kernels (kernel selection chooses narrow-kernel path), increasing handshake frequency and more memcpys overall. both increase chance of serialization.

devon: can you repro on a pinned-core dev box with isolcpus? if isolating the prefetch thread removes the gap, it's CPU scheduling. Also try setting that thread to SCHED_FIFO on a test host.

sara: I tried a quick experiment: nice -20 on prefetch reduced wakeups from ~1.2ms to ~40-80us on a dev box; tail P95 dropped ~18%. still seeing production tail in k8s hosts though.

nate: for kernel selection - if the runtime picks the narrow-kernel (faster per-op but higher kernel-count) the number of handshakes increases. can we test with forced kernel variant switch to the wider kernel (fewer launches) to compare?

sara: plan: 1) run perfetto with 1ms granularity to capture CPU wakeups + nsight waterfalled; 2) run controlled test toggling kernel-variant to measure overlap; 3) try swapping prefetch to dedicated pinned-host thread with CPU affinity. I'll upload traces to s3.

devon: I can flip batcher.coalesce_window and batcher.max_inflight to see if coalescing reduces small-kernel churn. also will test moving prefetch to a single copy-engine stream and using cudaEvent handoff instead of hostspin busy-poll.

perf-bot: nsys export uploaded: s3://redwood-traces/1798765432-hostspin-kvcache-interf.tar.gz

eva: :thumbsup: nice repro notes. let's sync and review traces tomorrow 11:00 — priorities: verify CPU-sched vs stream-mapping, quantify kernel-count impact, and draft mitigations (affinity + coalescing + copy-engine routing).

sara: one more micro-observation: in the trace there are short bursts where two H2D copies queue up back-to-back with no intervening kernel; those bursts coincide with a kernel that used a small-kernel codepath earlier. suggests heuristics or quantization changed the kernel-selection boundary. I'll annotate those ranges in the trace (prefetch-handshake tags).

devon: good call. I'll try an experiment that forces prefetch to use non-blocking host-to-device copies with a reserved pinned-pool and see if that reduces visible hostspin. also will add a tracepoint in the batcher at handshake start/end.

sara: thanks — uploading annotated perfetto slices now. if anyone wants to poke the run id directly: 1798765432.
